text.tspan: Two clusters, both VPCs are 10.0.0.0/16: private NAT gateway + Transit Gateway
Node and pod subnets (10.0.x.x, NOT routable outside)
Node and pod subnets (10.0.x.x, NOT routable outside)
Why plain peering / TGW fail: in each VPC the local route (10.0.0.0/16 → local) always wins, so 10.0.x.x can never mean 'the other VPC'.
Fix: only unique, routable addresses cross the TGW. Outbound, the private NAT hides pod A behind 10.100.0.5.
Inbound, the NLB in the routable subnet is the only address A can reach in B. Replies retrace the same path (NAT keeps connection state).
B → A needs the mirror image (private NAT in B, NLB in A). Easier per-service options: VPC Lattice or PrivateLink.
